creates_law_reviewed.class: VERIFICATION -- it re-derives a forwarded seat's six sweeps on this bench; the findings, such as they are, belong to the sweeps and to the arcs they audit.
creates_law_reviewed.basis: The one thing here that is not a re-derivation is the STRATIFICATION of sweep 6 by generator count, which refines someone else's finding rather than establishing a new general proposition. If the stratum law (a declining 2-generator stratum against a flat 3-generator one) is wanted as a law it should be posed and registered on its own arc, over more than three slices.

claim_one_line: THE SIX SWEEPS INTAKEN: THE HEADLINE REPRODUCES TO EVERY DIGIT AND IS AN UNDERSTATEMENT, THE ABSENT-TERM LIST IS RIGHT ON MAIN WHILE EIGHT OF ITS SIXTEEN TERMS ARE ALREADY PRESENT ON THIS BRANCH, AND ONE ABSENCE SURVIVES A DIACRITIC TRAP. Incoming chat1_SWEEPS_2026-09-12: a six-sweep audit plus two scripts, every number RECOMPUTED here and nothing read from the report. SWEEP 6, the finding: the 2T-surjection rate pi_1(M) ->> SL(2,3) against census depth reproduces EXACTLY on all six numbers -- 34.25% at mean volume 4.183 on [0:800], 29.38% at 4.767 on [20000:20800], 21.12% at 5.650 on [80000:80800] -- and B993's cornerstone control reproduces exactly too, m004 carrying 48 raw surjections, /|Aut(2T)| = 24 -> exactly 2. THE CONFOUND I WENT LOOKING FOR IS NOT THERE: their instrument silently skips presentations with more than 3 generators and reports neither n nor the skip count, and generator count correlates with complexity, which is the very variable the finding is about -- but skipped = 0 at all three slices, all 2400 manifolds having at most 3 generators, so the number is clean. BUT STRATIFYING BY GENERATOR COUNT REFINES IT AND SHOWS THE AGGREGATE UNDERSTATES IT: among 2-GENERATOR groups the rate runs 34.23% (n=745) -> 28.72% (n=679) -> 15.36% (n=534), two-proportion z = +7.56; among 3-GENERATOR groups it is FLAT at 34.55% (n=55) -> 33.06% (n=121) -> 32.71% (n=266), z = +0.26; and the 3-generator share grows 6.9% -> 15.1% -> 33.2%. THE DECLINE LIVES ENTIRELY IN THE 2-GENERATOR STRATUM, so the aggregate 34% -> 21% is a blend of a 34% -> 15% collapse with a flat 33%, and the growing non-declining stratum PROPS THE AGGREGATE UP: the effect where it acts is more than twice the headline. This sharpens their own standing note -- slicing at depth is necessary and NOT SUFFICIENT, since a depth slice still mixes strata moving in different directions; stratify by presentation complexity as well. THEIR READING OF B993 IS CORRECT INCLUDING THE DIRECTION: B993's ~1 in 3 is on a 400-manifold front sample which B993 STATES IN ITS OWN TEXT, so it is right for its declared sample; the census-wide rate is lower, the atom is rarer and m004 more distinguished, and the bias runs AGAINST the programme's own skepticism, inflating nothing. B993 is NOT corrected. Their self-retracted '1 in 3427' statistic appears as a standalone number in ZERO files of our prose or verdicts, so there is nothing to withdraw here. SWEEP 1 EXACT: CLAIMS.md 231 lines, 'base rate' 0, 'prereg' 0, 'control' 3, 'generic' 4, all five. SWEEP 3 REPRODUCES: arcs never mentioned anywhere = 0 (my 1226 arcs / 1359 ids against their 1240 / 1386 -- the difference is the COMMIT, this clone carrying branch-only arcs, not the method); they had predicted orphans, found none, and said so. SWEEP 4 VERIFIED on all five claims: P53 declares 'among the ten exceptional fillings', P48 names the imaginary-quadratic trace fields with floor -4, P10 carries its own demotion 'NOT an independent proof' plus NEEDS-SPECIALIST verbatim, P43 and P46 carry dated 2026-07-15 corrections. SWEEP 5: a TOOLING CORRECTION OF MINE FIRST -- I re-ran with git grep -ilw and got L-space = 0 against their 16, because -w fails on HYPHENATED terms; with their -il it is exactly 16, so their flag was right and mine was wrong. 12 of 13 COVERED counts then reproduce exactly; ONE DIFFERS, Bianchi, where they report 29 and the measurement is 115 -- an error in their table, immaterial since the term is covered on either count. All 16 ABSENT terms confirmed at 0 on origin/main. BUT EIGHT ARE ALREADY PRESENT ON THIS BRANCH: Kronheimer, ADHM, Nakajima, quiver variety, elliptic surface and minimal resolution from B1343, waist size from B1345, Minahan-Nemeschansky in the views -- and the precedent they cite for the yield HAS ALREADY PAID OUT, since B1345 used exactly Adams 2002 waist size and Callahan 2009 uniqueness and found J(m004) = 1 IS B309's banked unit obstruction from the other side. This is a CROSS-SEAT VISIBILITY problem and not an error by either side: they audit origin/main, correctly and conservatively, while the answering work sits unmerged on this branch -- the same class as E71 (branch-local numbering) and E53 (a banked result not reaching the surfaces), since a seat cannot audit what has not landed. A NEAR-MISS OF MY OWN, RECORDED: their list has 'Jorgensen inequality' at 0, and I read that as an E54 false absence because 'Jorgensen' with the Danish o-slash returns 9 files on origin/main -- the exact shape of the E54 instance already in the ledger. I WAS WRONG AND CHECKED BEFORE REPORTING IT: all nine hits are ANDERSEN-JORGENSEN (arXiv:1206.2552, TQFT and Gauss sums), a DIFFERENT PERSON from Troels Jorgensen of the Kleinian-group inequality, so their absence claim holds at TOPIC level and not merely as a phrase. E72 shape, one name two people. SWEEP 2's located facts verify: B993's 400-manifold sample stated in-arc, B1330's 952 in-domain sectors, and v2873 recorded PROTECTED in our own B1346 F1 table. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: nothing reaches CLAIMS.md, F2 or Gate 5, and no value is read against any measurement. The eight now-present terms are a VISIBILITY note and not a claim that the blind spot is closed -- B1343's own verdict is that deriving those faces is FREE AND THEREFORE EVIDENTIALLY EMPTY, and B1345's Jorgensen number is a RE-DERIVATION of B309. THE TERRITORY HAS BEEN ENTERED; IT HAS NOT YET PAID.
